issue_context.title: Optimize storage for IcuLocaleData data
issue_context.body:
The massive string which is declared in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e2099f62f1ee28241f857edaf0ef7420018d11d8/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/IcuLocaleData.cs#L32 is cost close to 10kb on the disc. It should be possible to optimize this to reduce the size as the data are in a very narrow range (low case ASCII only).

@eerhardt

@marek-safar do you suggest we compress it and expand it at runtime? I think we can store it as ASCII encoding or store it as compressed binary and expand it at runtime.
@tarekgh I think suggestion might be to use UTF-8 or ASCII rather than UTF-16, that should remove almost half of the bytes

review_comments: Could the name that comes in here ever be provided by a caller, such that (in an erroneous case) this could crash with a stack overflow?
No, there is check for length 2 lines above https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/45296/files#diff-423b39c173efa91a947f7f39560ae5aa07a690040b4cc6438240107df45bdda9R3845
No, it has very complicated dependencies and it's not used by anything else. We could move it to `ASCIIUtility` later if there is another use for it.
These overflow `0x1007f` and are truncated `0x007f`; working on a fix
